transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I've been having this issue late at night. Once I start picking at the leftovers in the kitchen, it just feels like the sensible part of my brain is saying, 'That’s enough, Alejandro,' but my hand just keeps going back for more anyway. I just can't seem to stop myself once I start, and it's really starting to bother me.
During these late-night episodes, would you say you're eating a noticeably larger amount of food than most people would eat in that same short period of time?

Yes, I would. Some nights after supper... well, when I'm supposed to be putting away the leftover tamales or the mole, I’ll end up eating several servings right then and there. And then I'll usually take some pan dulce out to the garage and eat that, too. It's definitely a lot more food than I’d ever put on a plate if my family was actually there watching me.
Do these eating episodes typically happen when you wake up in the middle of the night, or are they occurring before you go to sleep in the evening?

It's before I go to sleep. I don't really wake up in the middle of the night to eat. Like I was saying, it usually happens right after supper when I'm cleaning up the kitchen for the night, so I haven't even gone to bed yet. Once I finally do get to sleep, I usually just stay asleep.
Over the past few months, how many nights per week would you say these overeating episodes have been happening?

Well, looking back... these late-night leftover episodes have been happening at least once most weeks. Often it's two nights a week. I guess I've noticed it's been going on like that ever since my cousin moved in with us.
You mentioned this started after your cousin moved in—about how many months ago was that, so I can get a sense of how long these episodes have been going on?
Well, he moved in about four months ago. So, yeah, I'd say this has been going on for right around four months.
After one of these late-night eating episodes, do you typically feel a strong sense of guilt, disgust with yourself, or embarrassment about how much you ate?

No, not really. I mean, I know I probably shouldn't be eating all those leftovers right after supper, but... I don't sit there feeling disgusted with myself or guilty about it. It's just something I end up doing, and then I go to bed.
Do you tend to eat these late-night portions alone or hide it from your family specifically because you feel embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Well, yes, I do make sure to eat alone. I usually wait until the house is completely quiet, or I'll take the food out to the garage. I just... I'd be embarrassed for my cousin or my family to see how much I'm putting away. I'm supposed to be the disciplined one in the house, you know? So I just keep it to myself.
After eating these large amounts of food at night, do you ever try to make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, skipping meals the next day, or exercising extra hard?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never tried to throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. And I don't skip meals the next day or go crazy with exercise. Like I said, I just kind of eat it and then go to bed. I don't really do anything to try and undo it afterwards.

latest_inference.note: Absence of guilt/disgust after episodes and lack of marked distress argues against full Binge-Eating Disorder (F50.81); pattern of recurrent large evening/pre-sleep eating with loss of control, hidden due to embarrassment, but no compensatory behaviors, fits best with Night Eating Syndrome, classified as Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder (F50.89). This is more specific than unspecified (F50.9).
